reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement with dose-dependent pharmacokinetics showing Cmax ranging from 178 ng/mL at 100 mg to 1500 ng/mL at 450 mg. This demonstrates systemic exposure and drug availability. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear evidence of estrogen receptor pathway modulation with increased endometrial thickness (4.079 mm at week 12, 5.400 mm at week 36) and uterine volume (66.822 mL at week 12, 41.083 mL at week 36). These are classic estrogen receptor agonist effects, suggesting the compound is engaging the receptor, though the direction suggests partial agonism rather than pure antagonism. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint was met with 20.2% ORR in the Phase 2 arm, which represents clinical benefit in this heavily pretreated population. The dose escalation arm showed 16.7% ORR. PFS was 4.6 months in both arms, showing disease control. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported, but the overall population of ER+ HER2- metastatic breast cancer patients showed response. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm trial without a control group, but the ORR of 20.2% is clinically meaningful in this setting. Safety was manageable with 450 mg established as the recommended dose after DLTs at 600 mg.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm design without historical control makes it difficult to definitively assess efficacy magnitude, though the 20.2% ORR appears clinically meaningful
